# This workflow will install Python dependencies, run tests and lint with a single version of Python
# For more information see: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/automating-builds-and-tests/building-and-testing-python

name: Test

on:
  push:
    branches: ["main", "next"]
  pull_request:
    branches: ["main", "next"]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  checks: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Python 3.12
        uses: actions/setup-python@v3
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v4
        with:
          enable-cache: true
          cache-dependency-glob: "uv.lock"
      - name: Cache uv dependencies
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cache/uv
            .venv
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-uv-${{ hashFiles('uv.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-uv-
      - name: Install dependencies
        run: |
          uv sync
      - name: Run pre-commit
        run: |
          uv run pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage pre-commit
      # - name: Lint with flake8
      #   run: |
      #     # stop the build if there are Python syntax errors or undefined names
      #     flake8 . --count --select=E9,F63,F7,F82 --show-source --statistics
      #     # exit-zero treats all errors as warnings. The GitHub editor is 127 chars wide
      #     flake8 . --count --exit-zero --max-complexity=10 --max-line-length=127 --statistics
      - name: Check environment variables
        run: |
          if [ -z "${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" ]; then
            echo "Error: OPENAI_API_KEY is not set in repository secrets"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "${{ secrets.LIVEKIT_API_KEY_SIMULATION }}" ]; then
            echo "Error: LIVEKIT_API_KEY_SIMULATION is not set in repository secrets"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "${{ secrets.LIVEKIT_API_SECRET_SIMULATION }}" ]; then
            echo "Error: LIVEKIT_API_SECRET_SIMULATION is not set in repository secrets"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ -z "${{ secrets.LIVEKIT_URL_SIMULATION }}" ]; then
            echo "Error: LIVEKIT_URL_SIMULATION is not set in repository secrets"
            exit 1
          fi
      - name: Test with pytest and generate coverage
        env:
          OPENAI_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}
          LIVEKIT_API_KEY_SIMULATION: ${{ secrets.LIVEKIT_API_KEY_SIMULATION }}
          LIVEKIT_API_SECRET_SIMULATION: ${{ secrets.LIVEKIT_API_SECRET_SIMULATION }}
          LIVEKIT_URL_SIMULATION: ${{ secrets.LIVEKIT_URL_SIMULATION }}
        run: |
          make test-cov

      - name: Generate coverage summary
        if: always()
        run: |
          echo "## Coverage Summary" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          echo "" >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY
          uv run python scripts/check_coverage.py >> $GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY || true

      - name: Coverage Report
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: py-cov-action/python-coverage-comment-action@v3
        with:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          MINIMUM_GREEN: 85
          MINIMUM_ORANGE: 70
          ANNOTATE_MISSING_LINES: true
          ANNOTATION_TYPE: warning

      - name: Upload coverage HTML report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: coverage-report
          path: htmlcov/
          retention-days: 7

	op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run agent start

# Test environment
# Usage: make test          # Run all tests (excluding simulation directories)
# Usage: make test path=... # Run specific test file
test:
	@if [ -n "$(path)" ]; then \
		op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run pytest -vvvv -s $(path); \
	else \
	    op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run pytest -n auto -v -s --ignore-glob="**/simulation*"; \
	fi

# Run simulation tests only
# Usage: make simulation    # Run all simulation tests
run-simulation:
	op run --env-file="./envs/development.env" -- uv run pytest -n auto -v -s tests/ -k "simulation" --maxfail=1 --tb=short --reruns=3 --reruns-delay=1

# Coverage Report with CI tool
test-cov:
	uv run pytest -s -vvvvv -n 2 --reruns 1 --ignore-glob="**/simulation*" --cov-report=xml --cov-report=html --cov-report=term-missing --cov .

# Inject environment variables from file to .env
# Works on MAC OSX only due to sed -i ''

Based on the search results, I can provide you with comprehensive information about using semantic-release with GitHub Actions when you have protected branches and are encountering the GH006 error.

## The Problem

When semantic-release tries to push to a protected branch, you'll encounter the error: "GH006: Protected branch update failed". This happens because "At least 1 approving review is required by reviewers with write access" or other branch protection rules are in place.

## Solutions to Bypass Branch Protection for Semantic Release

### 1. **Using a GitHub App (Recommended)**

By using GitHub Apps, you can get around this issue more safely. Install a GitHub App and permit it to perform a force push to the protected branches. It will allow the app to bypass the branch protection without managing secrets or Personal Access Tokens.

### 2. **Using Deploy Keys**

Add a public SSH key as a deploy key at Your repo -> Settings -> Security -> Deploy keys, check "Allow write access". Such deployment key is not tied to any account, but gives full write access including bypassing branch protection rules: Deploy keys with write access can perform the same actions as an organization member with admin access.

### 3. **Using Personal Access Token (PAT)**

You can use GitHub Personal Access Tokens (PATs) to authenticate as an administrator with permission to override the branch protection. This option is not very safe and requires more secret management.

For GitHub Actions, you need to set the token option of the actions/checkout action with a Personal Access Token with the repo permissions scope:

```yaml
- name: Checkout
  uses: actions/checkout@v3
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
    token: ${{ secrets.CI_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

### 4. **Using Repository Rules Instead of Branch Protection**

The situation around this is better than it was previously. The recommendation is to configure repository-rules instead of traditional branch protection because it offers better flexibility for defining bypass rules more granularly than traditional branch protection rules.

### 5. **Allow Bypass in Branch Protection Settings**

Under Protect matching branches, select Require a pull request before merging. The last checkbox option is "Allow specified actors to bypass required pull requests". However, this wouldn't be secure as the GitHub Actions user isn't branch specific. So adding it to this list would mean that anyone could push from any branch using a workflow and bypass all branch protection rules.

## Important Considerations

If you have branch protection rules configured to prevent pushes to your release branch and are making commits that are to be pushed back to that branch as part of the release, semantic-release cannot perform any magic to bypass those rules on its own. If you decide to make commits as part of your release, you have to account for that in your rule definition.

Creating pull requests for new releases is an option but is cumbersome and hinders automatic deployments because you need to approve the PR.

The most secure and recommended approach is using GitHub Apps or repository rules, as they provide better control and security compared to using Personal Access Tokens or completely disabling branch protection.

Based on the search results, I can provide you with comprehensive information about using semantic-release with GitHub Actions when you have protected branches and are encountering the GH006 error.

## The Problem

When semantic-release tries to push to a protected branch, you'll encounter the error: "GH006: Protected branch update failed". This happens because "At least 1 approving review is required by reviewers with write access" or other branch protection rules are in place.

## Solutions to Bypass Branch Protection for Semantic Release

### 1. **Using a GitHub App (Recommended)**

By using GitHub Apps, you can get around this issue more safely. Install a GitHub App and permit it to perform a force push to the protected branches. It will allow the app to bypass the branch protection without managing secrets or Personal Access Tokens.

### 2. **Using Deploy Keys**

Add a public SSH key as a deploy key at Your repo -> Settings -> Security -> Deploy keys, check "Allow write access". Such deployment key is not tied to any account, but gives full write access including bypassing branch protection rules: Deploy keys with write access can perform the same actions as an organization member with admin access.

### 3. **Using Personal Access Token (PAT)**

You can use GitHub Personal Access Tokens (PATs) to authenticate as an administrator with permission to override the branch protection. This option is not very safe and requires more secret management.

For GitHub Actions, you need to set the token option of the actions/checkout action with a Personal Access Token with the repo permissions scope:

```yaml
- name: Checkout
  uses: actions/checkout@v3
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
    token: ${{ secrets.CI_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
```

### 4. **Using Repository Rules Instead of Branch Protection**

The situation around this is better than it was previously. The recommendation is to configure repository-rules instead of traditional branch protection because it offers better flexibility for defining bypass rules more granularly than traditional branch protection rules.

### 5. **Allow Bypass in Branch Protection Settings**

Under Protect matching branches, select Require a pull request before merging. The last checkbox option is "Allow specified actors to bypass required pull requests". However, this wouldn't be secure as the GitHub Actions user isn't branch specific. So adding it to this list would mean that anyone could push from any branch using a workflow and bypass all branch protection rules.

## Important Considerations

If you have branch protection rules configured to prevent pushes to your release branch and are making commits that are to be pushed back to that branch as part of the release, semantic-release cannot perform any magic to bypass those rules on its own. If you decide to make commits as part of your release, you have to account for that in your rule definition.

Creating pull requests for new releases is an option but is cumbersome and hinders automatic deployments because you need to approve the PR.

The most secure and recommended approach is using GitHub Apps or repository rules, as they provide better control and security compared to using Personal Access Tokens or completely disabling branch protection.

name: Create Release PR

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
    paths-ignore:
      - 'CHANGELOG.md'
      - 'pyproject.toml'

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write

jobs:
  create-release-pr:
    name: Create Release PR
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Don't run on release commits themselves
    if: |
      !contains(github.event.head_commit.message, 'chore(release):') &&
      !contains(github.event.head_commit.message, '[skip ci]')
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v4
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync

      - name: Check for existing release PR
        id: check-pr
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          # Find existing open release PRs
          EXISTING_PR=$(gh pr list --label "release" --state open --json number,headRefName --jq '.[0]')
          
          if [ -n "$EXISTING_PR" ]; then
            PR_NUMBER=$(echo $EXISTING_PR | jq -r '.number')
            BRANCH_NAME=$(echo $EXISTING_PR | jq -r '.headRefName')
            
            echo "Found existing release PR #$PR_NUMBER on branch $BRANCH_NAME"
            echo "existing_pr=$PR_NUMBER" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            echo "existing_branch=$BRANCH_NAME" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            
            # Close the existing PR
            gh pr close $PR_NUMBER --comment "Closing in favor of new release PR"
            
            # Delete the branch
            git push origin --delete $BRANCH_NAME || true
          else
            echo "No existing release PR found"
            echo "existing_pr=" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          fi

      - name: Get next version
        id: get-version
        run: |
          # Run semantic-release in dry-run mode to get the next version
          NEXT_VERSION=$(uv run semantic-release version --print) || true
          
          if [ -z "$NEXT_VERSION" ] || [ "$NEXT_VERSION" = "No release will be made." ]; then
            echo "No new release needed"
            echo "new_version=" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
            exit 0
          fi
          
          echo "Next version will be: $NEXT_VERSION"
          echo "new_version=$NEXT_VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Create release branch
        if: steps.get-version.outputs.new_version != ''
        run: |
          VERSION=${{ steps.get-version.outputs.new_version }}
          BRANCH_NAME="release/v$VERSION"
          
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          
          # Create and checkout new branch
          git checkout -b $BRANCH_NAME
          
          echo "branch_name=$BRANCH_NAME" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Update version and changelog
        if: steps.get-version.outputs.new_version != ''
        run: |
          VERSION=${{ steps.get-version.outputs.new_version }}
          
          # Run semantic-release to update files (without committing/pushing)
          uv run semantic-release version --no-commit --no-tag --no-push --no-vcs-release
          
          # Stage changes
          git add pyproject.toml CHANGELOG.md
          
          # Commit changes
          git commit -m "chore(release): $VERSION
          
          Automatically generated by python-semantic-release"

      - name: Push release branch
        if: steps.get-version.outputs.new_version != ''
        run: |
          git push origin ${{ env.branch_name }}

      - name: Create Pull Request
        if: steps.get-version.outputs.new_version != ''
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          VERSION=${{ steps.get-version.outputs.new_version }}
          
          # Create PR with specific labels and title
          gh pr create \
            --base main \
            --head ${{ env.branch_name }} \
            --title "chore(release): v$VERSION" \
            --body "## 🚀 Release v$VERSION
          
          This PR contains the version bump and changelog for the next release.
          
          ### Changes
          - Updated version in \`pyproject.toml\` to $VERSION
          - Updated \`CHANGELOG.md\` with recent commits

          2. Merge this PR to trigger the release

             - Create GitHub release
          
          ---
          *This PR was automatically generated by the release workflow.*" \

name: Tag Release

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [closed]
    branches:
      - main

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  tag-release:
    name: Tag and Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Only run when a PR with 'release' label is merged
    if: |
      github.event.pull_request.merged == true &&
      contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'release') &&
      startsWith(github.event.pull_request.head.ref, 'release/')
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: main
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Setup Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v4
        with:
          enable-cache: true

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: uv sync

      - name: Extract version from PR
        id: extract-version
        env:
          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
          PR_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
        run: |
          # Extract version from PR title (format: "chore(release): vX.Y.Z")
          if [[ "$PR_TITLE" =~ v([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+) ]]; then
            VERSION="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
          # Fallback: extract from branch name (format: "release/vX.Y.Z")
          elif [[ "$PR_BRANCH" =~ v([0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+) ]]; then
            VERSION="${BASH_REMATCH[1]}"
          else
            echo "❌ Could not extract version from PR title or branch"
            exit 1
          fi
          
          echo "Extracted version: $VERSION"
          echo "version=$VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "tag=v$VERSION" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure git
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      - name: Create and push tag
        id: create-tag
        run: |
          TAG=${{ steps.extract-version.outputs.tag }}
          
          # Check if tag already exists
          if git rev-parse "$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "❌ Tag $TAG already exists"
            exit 1
          fi
          
          # Create annotated tag
          git tag -a "$TAG" -m "Release $TAG
          
          Automatically generated from PR #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}"
          
          # Push tag
          git push origin "$TAG"
          
          echo "✅ Created and pushed tag $TAG"

      - name: Read CHANGELOG for release notes
        id: changelog
        run: |
          VERSION=${{ steps.extract-version.outputs.version }}
